name: wifi-sta
description: Wi-Fi client (station mode): the MMI 3G+ joins a phone hotspot (WPA2-PSK) instead of running the car's access point, and the factory LAN mode routes online services through it. Ships a new 88W8688 station driver, wpa_supplicant 2.11 and Marvell's linux-firmware station firmware; the factory driver cannot do station mode.
author: chundla
scripts: wifi_sta_run.sh - check the card and the unit's factory files, set the LAN-mode flag, install the station files on the HDD, store wifi-sta/hotspot.conf, add the WifiClient GEM screen and the start-up block; or remove it all (wifi-sta/REMOVE on the card)

hardware.phone: A phone hotspot on 2.4 GHz with WPA2-PSK (iPhone: Maximise Compatibility on)
hardware.way_back_in: Station mode removes the car's access point until a restart; the GEM's 'Start-up: car access point' then a restart brings it back

notes: Validated on one unit only: 9411, HN+R_US_AU_K0942_3, MU 1038 (2012 Audi A6, North America). The installer refuses unless the factory devnp-mv8688uap.so, dhcp.client and dhcp-up match that unit's checksums, so other firmware is left untouched.

installs_to_flash is false so the builder does not copy scripts or platform.sh to efs-system. The module's own scripts write two things on flash: the WifiClient.esd screen in /mnt/efs-system/engdefs and a five-line marked block in /mnt/efs-system/lsd/lsd.sh, each with a backup and its own rollback. The station files go on the HDD (about 1 MB).
Needs the GEM enabled (gem-activator) to use the screen. SSH over the hotspot is optional and needs chundla/qnx632-openssh installed.
